question.text: The Embargo Act worsened America's international standing in the lead-up to this conflict. This war, named for the year in which it began, included the burning of Washington D.C. by the British and the Battle of New Orleans.
question.clue: Northern Federalists discussed succession at the Hartford Convention during this war.

swap.text: This second president of the US was the only president ever officially elected as a Federalist.
swap.answerHtml: John Adams [do not accept or prompt on “John Quincy Adams”]
swap.clue: As part of his efforts to expand the navy, he commissioned the USS Constitution, though he avoided using it to expand the Quasi-War.

question.leadin: Answer the following about lopsided Presidential victories.
question.text: This President continued the "Era of Good Feelings" by running for re-election unopposed in 1820. His namesake Doctrine declared that further European colonization efforts in the Western Hemisphere would be viewed as aggression against the U.S.
question.clue: During his presidency, slavery was outlawed above the thirty-sixth parallel in the Missouri Compromise.

swap.leadin: This event included the death of Oliver Miller, followed by the burning of John Neville's house.
swap.text: Name this 1794 Pennsylvanian rebellion that occurred in response to an excise tax on a particular liquor.
swap.clue: Future Treasury Secretary Albert Gallatin failed to prevent this event, an uprising that was sparked by the Report on Manufactures and Alexander Hamilton's policies.

question.text: This man's brother Tenskwatawa led the Native American forces at the Battle of Tippecanoe. Later, this Shawnee leader was killed by Richard Mentor Johnson at the Battle of the Thames during his war.
question.clue: Supposedly killed by future Vice-President Richard M. Johnson, it was this leader's troops, supplemented by British forces under Isaac Brock, that scared away William Hull, leading to the 1812 capture of Detroit.

swap.leadin: This president garnered the nickname "Old Rough and Ready" for his exploits in the Second Seminole War.
swap.text: Name this U.S. president who served as a general in the Mexican-American War. He was succeeded by Millard Fillmore after his death in office.
swap.clue: This man defeated Winfield Scott as the Whig candidate in the U.S. presidential election of 1848.

question.text: This coauthor of the Federalist papers was embroiled in the Reynolds scandal, and use his influence to tilt the election of 1800 in favor of Jefferson over Aaron Burr after the failure of his proposed candidate, Charles Pinckney.
question.clue: A report by this thinker called for the redemption of government securities and the assumption of state debts.

swap.leadin: This man lost to Andrew Jackson in 1832 as the Whig Party's first Presidential candidate.
swap.text: Name this longstanding Kentucky Senator, a "Great Compromiser" who ironed out the Missouri Compromise and Compromise of 1850 at the ends of a career in which he feuded with John C. Calhoun and Daniel Webster.
swap.clue: Early on he worked under George Wythe and married Lucretia Hart, settling down on his estate of Ashland.

question.text: It became heated in the winter of 1838 and 1839, when Canadian lumberjacks used the disputed area for logging and seized an American land agent. For 15 points, name this conflict between citizens of Maine and New Brunswick.
question.clue: That led Governor Robert Dunlap to issue a general order announcing they had been invaded by a foreign power.

swap.text: In the 1830s, the Whigs and Henry Clay in particular pushed this threefold economic plan, which sought to establish a protective tariff, a national bank, and subsidies for internal improvements such as roads and canals.
swap.clue: The passing of the Tariff of 1816 and the creation of the Second Bank of the United States are considered major wins for this policy program.

question.leadin: Answer the following about historically significant American roads.
question.text: A funding bill for this road situated entirely within Kentucky was controversially vetoed by Andrew Jackson, who allegedly did so to spite his Kentuckian rival Henry Clay.
question.clue: As part of his rivalry with Clay, Jackson vetoed a bill to fund this proposed road linking Lexington, Kentucky to the namesake city on the Ohio river, limiting the success of the American System.

swap.leadin: This man's Western name was Billy Powell.
swap.text: Name this Florida tribal leader who was captured by Thomas Jesup after being promised a flag of truce for negotiations in 1837.
swap.clue: Quartermaster General Thomas Jesup captured Micanopy and this man under a false white flag, after which he died in captivity of an abscess.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Louisiana Purchase.
question.text: This New York politician, who was nicknamed "the Chancellor," negotiated the Louisiana Purchase as the Minister to France.
question.clue: This person that negotiated the Louisiana Purchase while serving as the Minister to France. This person developed a viable steamboat while working with Robert Fulton.

swap.leadin: This man and his brother Pierre organized themselves on the island of Barataria.
swap.text: Name this pirate. Governor William Claiborne put out an order for his capture, and later, many of his supporters and ships were captured by Commodore Daniel Patterson, but he was eventually pardoned.
swap.clue: This man, with his older brother, Pierre, met with Andrew Jackson in December 1814 and offered his assistance for a battle which ended in January the following year.

question.text: The Supreme Court rejected the petitioners' argument that the creation of the Warren Bridge was in violation of this clause of the Constitution. This clause was also the basis for the decision in Fletcher v. Peck.
question.answerHtml: Contract Clause [or Article I, Section 10, Clause 1 of the Constitution]
question.clue: In order to prevent state governors from having authority to forgive debts, Hamilton pushed for this clause to be included in the Constitution. It also prohibits states from making treaties and was used as the basis of Fletcher vs. Peck.

swap.text: New York Democrats who, like David Wilmot, opposed the extension of slavery to the territories, were known by this name. These opponents of the Hunkers nominated Martin van Buren for the presidency in 1848.
swap.clue: This group of radical New York Democrats were named for an extreme method of killing rats and opposed by the Hunkers. Their objectives included preventing the extension of slavery and stopping abuses by corporations.

question.leadin: This man took out a personal loan to help pay for the War of 1812 after the New York State legislature refused to pony up the funds.
question.text: Identify this two-term vice president whose subsequent turn to alcoholism was due to a scandal involving that war loan. During his tenure as New York's Governor, the state agreed to abolish slavery within 10 years.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about a statesman FTSNOP.
swap.text: This essay, anonymously written in 1829, was composed in response to the "Tariff of Abominations" and fully expounded on the concept of nullification and states rights.
swap.clue: This document, a litany of complaints which circulated in response to the Tariff of 1828.

question.leadin: Answer stuff about xenophobic American legislation of the 1790s, FTPE.
question.text: This Federalist enforced the Alien and Sedition and Logan Acts. He was the third Secretary of State in American history, succeeding Edmund Randolph and serving from 1795 to 1800.
question.clue: As a colonel, he led an unsuccessful effort to cut off the British retreat from Lexington but was nonetheless made Quartermaster-General in 1780, having earlier published the Continental Army's first field manual.

swap.text: This man, who served as Andrew Jackson's Postmaster General, was a proponent of the New Court. This editor-in-chief of the Argus of Western America is sometimes cited as the first "unofficial" US Press Secretary.
swap.clue: He donated his home and property, known as his namesake "green," to serve as Gallaudet University for deaf children.
